chosen_format.why_it_works: borrows dating-red-flag language to make vetting feel personal instead of clinical. the list format invites the viewer to self-check against it in real time, and putting the brand as the single green flag at the end flips the whole list without ever pitching it directly
chosen_format.text_skeleton: red flags in a {PERSON_TYPE}: {RED_FLAG_1}. {RED_FLAG_2}. {RED_FLAG_3}. {RED_FLAG_4}. green flag: {ACTION_WITH_BRAND}
chosen_format.visual_mechanic: counting off red flags on raised fingers, exaggerated unimpressed head tilt

format_scores.reason: The self-check mechanic maps naturally onto the pain of buried bugs and Slack-switching chaos—engineers can immediately recognize each red flag in their own workflow—but the dating-language emotional register needs slight bending since Linear's tone is direct and opinionated rather than playful or personal.

The escalating negation list maps reasonably onto the alternatives (Jira, Notion, Slack threads) and the 'admired for refusing the easy path' mechanic fits Linear's opinionated tone, but the vulgar/psychopath framing clashes slightly with Linear's precise, professional register and the pain (buried bugs/notifications) is less a lifestyle-choice story than an operational frustration, requiring the format to be bent to feel authentic.

The gap-between-claim-and-mundane-reveal mechanic can work (e.g., 'thought I could ship a whole product solo… used Linear's AI triage… turns out I just had 47 buried bugs'), but the core pain of buried notifications and Slack/spreadsheet chaos is anxiety-driven rather than confidence-driven, so the 'delusional confidence' emotional register requires meaningful bending to feel authentic to Linear's direct, opinionated tone.

The self-deprecating 'unglamorous discipline' mechanic centers on personal lifestyle habits and humble-brag identity, but Linear's core pain is team coordination chaos and buried notifications—a professional workflow problem that doesn't map naturally onto the introspective, individualistic emotional register this format requires.

variants.text: red flags in a tech lead: still triaging bugs inside a jira board from 2019. pings the team in slack instead of updating the ticket. tracks sprint progress in a google sheet. hasn't closed a p0 in three weeks. green flag: caught triaging the backlog in linear at 7am before standup

red flags in an engineering manager: routes bug reports through a slack thread. keeps the roadmap in a notion doc nobody opens. calls a meeting to ask what's blocked. closes jira tickets by hand every friday. green flag: spotted letting linear triage the overnight alerts before anyone's logged on

red flags in a product manager: sprint board lives in a jira ticket graveyard. pings six people in slack to find who owns a bug. roadmap is a google sheet with three broken formulas. marks everything priority one. green flag: seen letting linear sort the incoming bug queue while the standup is still loading
variants.length_flag_reason: 54 words vs target 46 (+/-15% band: 39-53); closest of 2 attempts, kept rather than looping further

winner_reasoning: Variant 2 lands the hardest because 'google sheet with three broken formulas' and 'marks everything priority one' are painfully specific and universally recognized behaviors that feel lived-in, not written. The green flag payoff — 'while the standup is still loading' — earns a laugh and makes the product feel fast without saying fast.

creator_brief.audio_note: Fast-cut, dry-sarcastic lo-fi with a punchy snare and slightly off-kilter synth stabs — like a corporate satire sketch underscore at ~130 BPM in a minor key; this is the format's default mood, kept because the red-flag countdown format and tech-worker in-jokes are pure meme energy that matches Linear's opinionated, no-BS brand voice.

creator_brief.performance_note: Weaponized secondhand embarrassment — deadpan disgust at the red flags, delivered with each finger raised slowly and a flat, barely-blinking stare at camera, then a subtle smug exhale and half-smile on the green flag reveal.
